Lower bounds: all four expected origins are distinct, so each single-page slot-use serves exactly one destination; 4 slot-uses / 2 slots force >=2 rounds. A slot can hold only one pending read at a time, and round-2 reads cannot be issued until slots are freed by wait_writes+release (which is after round-1 wait_reads), so reads batch only within a round: publish requires an initialized value with no pending read and only blocking wait_reads observes read completion, giving >=1 wait_reads per round. Reuse requires release, which requires no pending transfer on the slot; since a non-wait op invalid at ANY reachable state is unsafe, wait_writes must precede each round's releases (writes precede every release), giving >=1 wait_writes per round. Hence >=4 waits; a 1-slot schedule would need 8, and extra slots are unavailable (slots=2). Command bound: each slot-use strictly needs reserve/read/publish/acquire/write/release (write needs acquired+initialized; acquire needs published; final state needs all slots free), i.e. 24 + 4 waits = 28; no op is droppable and one write cannot serve two distinct expected origins. Peak live slots is 2, the task's slot count, already minimal. Correctness: round 1 maps src2->dst0 and src0->dst1, round 2 maps src3->dst2 and src1->dst3, matching expected=[2,0,3,1]; reads target distinct slots, writes target distinct destinations, and every non-wait op is enabled under all completion orders, with no reliance on DMA finishing early."
